sections.content: The refactor acceptance skill requires frozen baselines, complete manifests, typed requests, action DAGs, command registries, custody, receipts, and hash-verified knowledge context. It supports evidence-only and controlled-validation modes, deterministic replay, controlled recovery, bounded semantic rounds, and fail-closed handling of unsafe or unsupported inputs. Acceptance does not imply release, archive, deploy, or commit.
sections.title: Acceptance Skills

sections.content: The VDD skill creates or repairs explicit execution-plan directories using standard, resumable, or self-hosted profiles. It requires authority references, integrity preflight, observable acceptance targets, recovery data, immutable repair history, and terminal validation. The cited completion report records implementation-complete status, closed toolchain policy work, three repair rounds, accepted ADR-0053, passing validator checks, and no release or acceptance outcome.
sections.title: Execution Plan And Report

sections.content: The implementation validator checks required artifacts and six registered commands, returning implementation-complete only when all checks pass. The command registry defines sixteen non-shell Python checks covering plan validation, skill replay, historical compatibility, acceptance package validation, downstream routing replay, and terminal validation. The implementation contract defines a self-hosted replay plan with detached positive and negative probes, stable-candidate matrices, sorted hashed manifests, constrained edits, preserved failure history, and no hidden backend state.
